National Assembly
Eklaisau Convention
Complete Details
Proceedings
Friday, Jestha 2083
Meeting Number -
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 1:18 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members,
(1:18 PM)
The proceedings of the National Assembly meeting commence. Honourable members, time has been requested to speak during the emergency hour. I have allocated a maximum of three minutes for each honourable member to speak during the emergency hour. I will now provide time to the honourable members in order.
First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:18 PM)
Sir, various hospitals have reported a shortage of Carboplatin and Cisplatin medicines used in the treatment of fatal diseases like cancer in Nepal. Doctors have warned that the treatment of cancer patients could be affected due to the shortage of these medicines used in chemotherapy. Due to the lack of medicine, patients who could have been cured of cancer may be deprived of treatment, leading to a serious public health crisis. Right Honourable Chairperson, this is not just a problem of emergency, it is a matter of life and death. Our Honourable Prime Minister does not even have time to speak, and has vowed to change the country miraculously by not speaking. As a result, the parliament is looking for a Prime Minister, but the Prime Minister is busy and silent.
Through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, I strongly demand that the Government of Nepal immediately supply the medicines and save the lives of cancer patients across the country. I express my sorrow over the incident that occurred regarding the border area between Bajura and Humla districts, Rani Sain, Lampata. I wish the injured in the incident a speedy recovery.
Right Honourable Chairperson, as the border issue between the two districts is a very sensitive matter, the state should form a high-level mechanism to resolve the problem related to the survey and maps of the area. However, today, due to the same incident, the national highway has been blocked one after another. Due to the blockage of the highway, ordinary citizens are forced to suffer unnecessarily. Especially patients travelling for treatment, students studying, and vehicles carrying food supplies are greatly affected by the blockage. Right Honourable Chairperson, the government has remained silent, turning a deaf ear, to the situation arising from such a sensitive incident as the border dispute. I draw the serious attention of the Government of Nepal, through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, to immediately normalize the situation, find a permanent solution, and open the blocked highway as soon as possible. What is the government doing about this, and what is the progress of the government in supplying the much-needed cancer medicine? I demand, through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, that the ministers of the respective ministries of the Government of Nepal be summoned to this esteemed house to provide an answer. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Renu Chand.
(1:21 PM)
Honourable Mr. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party):-
(1:21 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson,
Sir, there has been a dispute and clash in the Lampata, Chyachor area, which has immense potential for herbs and tourism. In the course of the clash, there was a physical altercation and beating among the local residents. The establishment of a police post has become a point of contention, and construction work has been halted. It is also being called a border dispute. Ward Chairman, Administrative Officer Kul Bahadur Thapa, Ward Member Pema Gara Gurung, his wife Laxmi Gurung, local Min Gurung, and Police Havildar Ramesh Dhami of Himali Rural Municipality-3 were physically assaulted and beaten. This area is not only a habitat for herbs but also for many rare wild animals including musk deer. Recently, there has also been an increase in tourists in this area. Sudurpaschim is already a virgin land from a tourism perspective, and recently tourists have started going there. A police post is necessary there for the security of tourists going to Ranisain. This is also an old route for smuggling, bordering Darchula, and smuggling has been happening from there. Bajura citizens have been living here since 2034 BS. Is it because of the border dispute that they are not allowing a police post to be established? I want to draw the attention of the Chairperson to the fact that the government should investigate this. I want to draw the attention of the government, through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, to the border dispute between the two districts, and also to the establishment of a police post for the security of tourists.
Another issue, Right Honourable Chairperson, Nepal's pharmaceutical industry is in ruins. The government must address this. The Government of Nepal should immediately manage imports and focus on resuming and managing domestic production, and I want to draw the attention of this esteemed house and the government, through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, to formulate policies for this. Although the absence and silence of the head of government make it uncertain how many of these issues will be addressed, I hope that the people's concerns will reach the government and that there will be a serious ruling on this matter through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, as I conclude my remarks. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Minasingh Rakhal.
(1:23 PM)
(Nepal Communist Party, UML):-
Honourable Mr. Minasingh Rakhal
(1:23 PM)
(Right Honourable Chairperson, Sir, in Ward No. 5 of Chankheli Rural Municipality in Humla district of Karnali Province, the severe rain and flood that occurred on the night of Jestha 4 caused the entire village to be swept away. Houses have been washed away, farmlands have been buried, drinking water and roads have been obstructed. Some families are forced to live under the open sky. It is reported that schools, health posts, and local structures have also suffered significant damage. But sadly, in such a disaster, the affected people have not felt the presence of the state. Relief and rescue, which should have reached immediately, have not yet been adequately arranged. Why does the government's attention reach late when a disaster strikes in remote Karnali? Why is the value of people's lives and suffering not equal? I demand from the government immediately. Rescue the affected families safely. Arrange for food, clothing, and temporary shelter. Collect the actual details of the damage and proceed with relief and reconstruction work immediately. Let the people not feel alone in natural disasters. Let the government show through its actions that the citizens of Karnali are also citizens with equal rights in this country. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members' turn to speak during the emergency hour concludes here. The names of honourable members to speak during the zero hour have been presented. I have allocated one minute to each honourable member to speak during the zero hour. First, Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson
(1:25 PM)
Sir, Article 86 (2) (a) of the Constitution of Nepal makes provisions regarding the formation of the National Assembly. It provides for the formation of the National Assembly with 59 members from various provinces. And in sub-section 5 of this article, it is provided that vacancies shall be filled in the same manner for the remaining term. Right Honourable Chairperson, out of the 59 members of the National Assembly of the Federal Parliament, two members have been vacant for the past six months. However, in this context, due to these vacancies, various difficulties are arising in the proceedings of the National Assembly. Therefore, through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, I strongly demand that the Government of Nepal and the Election Commission immediately commence the process of filling the remaining member seats. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Manrupa Sharma.
(1:26 PM)
Honourable Mr. Manrupa Sharma (Nepal Communist Party):- Right Honourable Chairperson
(1:26 PM)
Sir, the landless have been kept in holding centers. And children, the elderly, lactating mothers, and disabled individuals are experiencing more mental distress. They need counselling. And through you, Right Honourable Chairperson, I urge the Government of Nepal to provide them with counselling as soon as possible, and to persuade them quickly whether to keep them there or move them elsewhere? Counselling is needed. The government should provide counselling as soon as possible. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(1:27 PM)
Honourable Mr. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):
(1:28 PM)
India owes Nepali compensation for approximately 33,000 bighas of land that should have been given to Nepal for the construction of the Bharadah Koshi bridge. The government should take necessary initiatives. I want to say this through you, Chairperson. And I request that due to the constant inundation in the area around Laukahi and Bhantabari in the Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve in Sunsari district, there is also significant erosion. Farmers are terrified. I want to draw the government's attention. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Renu Chand.
(1:28 PM)
Honourable Mr. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(1:28 PM)
I have a question for the government, through you, Sir: Are these landless people Nepali citizens or not? If they are, then the government itself is responsible for protecting the human rights and fundamental rights of the displaced landless people. The central government has directly instructed the local government to use bulldozers. This is not in accordance with federalism. The responsibility for data collection should be given to the local government. Unauthorized bodies are being used for this. I want to draw attention to this as well. Landless people are being provided with rotten food and contaminated water. And our Prime Minister says "See cheese". While the landless are crying and the elderly are suffering without treatment, my question to the Honourable Prime Minister is "How can we see cheese" (... time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota.
(1:30 PM)
Honourable Mr. Vishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):-
(1:30 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson, according to the statistics of the Cooperative Department, there are 31,450 cooperatives across the country. Of these, approximately 24,000 cooperatives conduct savings and loan transactions. The department has so far declared 22 cooperatives as problematic. Among the cooperatives in crisis, the parliamentary inquiry committee has investigated the misappropriation in 40 cooperatives. However, the cooperative victims' "National Campaign Federation for Cooperative Savings and Protection" mentions that there are more than 14.5 million victims from 418 cooperatives nationwide. The government's decision to return the money of cooperative victims is welcome. But what is the state's source for returning the victims' money? Which source is being used? For transparency, I make a clear demand from the government through you, Right Honourable Chairperson. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Vishnu Devi Pudasaini.
(1:31 PM)
Honourable Mr. Vishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson
(1:31 PM)
Sir, it is not as easy to build and manage as it is to demolish, burn, and destroy. The problems caused by the bulldozer terror have worried everyone. So many bulldozers have demolished...

The pollution is increasing, and if foreign guests come and visit, take photos, and ask what is happening, what will Nepalis say? For that, I draw the government's attention through this esteemed house to arrange the destroyed and damaged places as soon as possible. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
(13:31 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal:-
(13:32 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson Sir, due to the continuous rainfall on the evening of Jestha 4th in Nepka village, Ward No. 4 of Chankheli Rural Municipality in Humla district, floods and landslides have destroyed half the village and a dozen houses. The school building has been washed away. Sheds have been destroyed. Hundreds of cows, oxen, and sheep have died there. Therefore, the villagers of Nepka are currently in distress. Students are unable to study. Therefore, I urge that the school in Nepka village be rebuilt as soon as possible and that arrangements be made quickly for the food, shelter, clothing, and security of the distressed community there.
I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal through the Honorable Chairperson. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari.
(13:32 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Communist Party of Nepal):-
(13:33 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson Sir, I request the house to be informed whether the amount the government has started to provide to cooperative victims is from the government treasury or if it is being collected from cooperative fraudsters and then provided to the cooperative victims. Another issue is that public debt has now exceeded 29 trillion and the gross domestic product (GDP) has exceeded 45 percent. If this situation worsens, institutions like the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank will impose strict conditions on loan assistance, and Nepal's financial autonomy will be curtailed. The new government, which claims the previous one drowned the country in debt, why is it rushing to take loans indiscriminately today? If loans are taken without a credible basis for investment in productive sectors, and if they are not spent on productive sectors, it can be a serious blow to the nation. What are the loans being taken for? (Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Savitri Malle.
(13:34 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Savitri Malle (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable
(13:34 hrs)
Chairperson Sir, in Jaljale, Bhairavi Rural Municipality, Dailekh district of Karnali Province, a Chinese company has completed petroleum exploration work spending approximately 2 billion rupees and has submitted a report to the Government of Nepal stating that there are approximately 1.12 billion cubic meters of gas in that location. If the production and distribution of this project are operationalized, Nepal can become self-reliant in gas and fuel, employment will be generated across the country, and national capital will be built. However, the second phase of this project is currently stalled. It appears that the government has not made adequate arrangements for this project, has not paid attention to it, it does not seem to be a priority in the government's policy, programs, and principles, and it has not been included in national pride projects. It is not being prioritized. Because in the budget ceiling of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies for 2083/084... (Time expired.)

(13:35 hrs)
Chairperson: Honorable
The program for honorable members to speak in Zero Hour concludes here. The names of honorable members have been proposed for speaking in Special Time based on party representation. Now I will provide time for honorable members to speak. First, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, time 15 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
(13:36 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson Sir, I seek permission to stand up in the esteemed house of the National Assembly today and express some views on contemporary and some political issues.
Honorable Chairperson Sir, it has been approximately 56-57 days since the government was formed. Generally, the first three months after a government is formed are called the honeymoon period, and during these three months, there is usually no significant criticism of the government. The practice is to let the government work at its own pace. We are also in that mindset. The Nepali Congress is also largely in that mindset. But the strange thing is, Honorable Chairperson Sir, the government, like a hungry person who hasn't eaten for ten days, has started grabbing food from all sides as soon as it arrived, as if it were extremely hungry. I do wish the government well. I want the government to do good work. We want to support your good and creative work. We will definitely support your good work in providing comfort and prosperity to the Nepali people. However, I also want the government to slow down a bit, to be a bit more mature and patient.
Honorable Chairperson Sir, one issue I want to raise is that whenever we have moved from the Stone Age to the Agricultural Age and then to the Social Age in Nepal, the need for cooperation between pairs has increased. Even when we formed social structures, we created such paired traditions. If we watch some movies, we see the pair of Amitabh Bachchan and our other hero in the Sholay film. In music, we see the good pairing of Narayan Gopal and Gopal Yonjan. A good example of this can be seen in cricket. The partnership and pairing of the batsmen there, especially Nepal's very popular batsman Dipendra Singh Airee, and then our Paudel ji, Rohit Paudel ji, their partnership is found to be very good. If we talk about films, in older films, the pairs of Shiva Shrestha and Bhuvan KC were very popular.
Now, let's look at how our pairings are in politics. Since I have less information about older pairs, I want to talk about more recent pairs.
Especially after the People's Movement of 2046/2047, when a new government was formed, the pairing of the respected leader Girija Prasad Koirala, the respected leader Ganesh Man Singh, and Krishna Prasad Bhattarai was seen to be very strong to some extent. Especially in 2056 BS, the Nepali Congress went to seek votes by presenting the pairing of respected leader Girija Prasad Koirala and Krishna Prasad Bhattarai. The Nepali people accepted that mandate, gave overwhelming votes, and the Nepali Congress was victorious. But when that mandate could not be maintained properly, leading to the events of 2058 BS, where did our political course lead? Now, rather than me discussing this, there are more distinguished individuals in this house who have experienced it. I just wanted to mention it as a reference.
Similarly, if we consider another notable pairing, when the general elections were held in 2074 BS, especially the pairing of the respected former Prime Minister KP Oli and the respected former Prime Minister Prachanda was able to convince the public greatly. For the first time in Nepal, the Communist Party received almost a two-thirds majority and moved towards the process of state governance. But within a few years of the people giving such votes, what happened to that pairing? It was said that we are two pilots, one main pilot and the other co-pilot, flying the ship of the country's prosperity. But when the understanding between these two pairs broke down, we here have direct knowledge and experience of the political turmoil this country fell into three years later.
Honorable Chairperson Sir, a similar period came in 2082 BS in Nepal's political history. After the Janajagaran movement and the movement of Bhadra 23 and 24, when we were in a situation where we had to go to snap elections, a pairing was formed very well overnight. Especially the pairing of the respected Prime Minister Balen Shah and the Chairman of Rastriya Swatantra Party, Rabi Lamichhane, was seen to be very strong. It was also seen that they were able to convince the public well. That vote was also seen in the elections of Falgun 29. And now we have reached this point. Honorable Chairperson Sir, what I want to highlight here is that whenever such pairings have managed the affairs of Nepal, they have not proven to be very successful. The pairing of 2056 BS, such a good pairing, such a historic pairing, a pairing with such unparalleled personalities, got entangled in petty interests, how did it reach the point of division due to small matters, and how did the situation arise where the respected former Prime Minister Krishna Prasad Bhattarai had to resign? We have seen it. The events of 2074 BS have already been mentioned. The pairing of Balen and Rabi, which came from the elections in 2082 BS, how this pairing will proceed, what this pairing will be like, is currently a topic of discussion among Nepali political analysts, the Nepali public, and those interested in Nepali politics. My analysis is that if those pairings cannot accept the spirit of coexistence, then those pairings will fail. In 2056 BS, if Girija Babu had accepted the leadership of Krishna Prasad Bhattarai, the coexistence of the coalition, and that politics, perhaps that accident would not have happened? In 2074 BS, if the respected former Prime Minister KP Oli had not underestimated the respected former Prime Minister Prachanda, whom he had declared as co-pilot, perhaps that political accident would not have happened? Now, the pairing of the respected Prime Minister Balen Shah, who is in the driving seat, and Rabi Lamichhane, appears to be compatible at first glance. However, whispers of discord are starting to be heard from within. You all know, when we see a ripe pumpkin from the outside, it looks very good. We don't see any worms. Until it reaches the point where it is so worm-eaten that it cannot be used, we don't see what is inside that pumpkin. My personal wish is that this latest pairing does not turn out that way. Nepal's politics does not seek pairings that do not respect coexistence. Nepal's politics does not seek politicians who cannot realize the responsibility of this time. Therefore, this pairing should realize the responsibility of the time and should be able to grasp the aspirations for development and prosperity that the time and the people have, and this pairing should be able to take collective responsibility to realize and bring it to fruition. Especially, this pairing should not become like the pairing of B.P. and Tulsi Giri. Especially, this pairing should not become like the pairing of Prachanda and Baburam. This pairing should not become like the pairing of KP and Bidya Devi Bhandari. I wish them well.
Honorable Chairperson Sir, I would also like to briefly enter into another topic. Especially since this government was formed on Chaitra 13th, the general public has started demanding that the members of the Council of Ministers of Nepal should publicly disclose their property details as per the Constitution of Nepal. When the members of the government's Council of Ministers disclosed their property details, the Nepali people were shocked. Ministers who came to the Janajagaran movement distributing water bottles are worth crores...

He turned out to be the owner of property worth crores. The Nepali people did not understand that. When the Nepali people saw the members of the Council of Ministers adorned with gold, I can only imagine how much they must have suffered. Honorable Chairperson, the point I want to emphasize here is that, first, according to Section 31 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2048, public office holders must submit their property details. That section needs to be amended to include the provision of disclosing the source of gold, silver, diamonds, and jewels. In this way, even five years after leaving the Council of Ministers, if a provision is made to declare accumulated property up to 200 tolas of gold as being from traditional sources, corruption will start from here. Therefore, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I would like to demand that Section 31 of the Prevention of Corruption Act related to the investigation of abuse of authority be amended. Honorable Chairperson, specifically, the former Home Minister had to resign from his post due to allegations of corruption and accumulating ill-gotten wealth. In this context, a committee has been formed under the convenorship of former Justice Achyut Prasad Bhandari to investigate this. I feel the government should not engage in such theatrics. The former Home Minister has already stated that he will emerge cleansed in a few days. He has already announced on social media that he will become the Home Minister again. The government is creating a commission to cleanse the minister, and it is doing such work. Such theatrics should not be done in a place with such wise individuals and politicians like you, and the source of the property that was publicly disclosed by all the members of the Council of Ministers should be disclosed in a way that the Nepali people can understand. I strongly demand this. My final point, Honorable Chairperson, the government has brought an ordinance and has removed more than 1534 public office holders from their positions. The government has said that we will make nominations based on merit. When I looked at the nominations made by the government, it seems that a former military officer has been nominated as the Chairman of the Bagmati Civilization Integrated Development Committee, which is endowed with authority. A former military officer has been placed first in the appointment of a board member of Nepal Airlines Corporation. I want to ask the government, Honorable Chairperson, through you, what is the ultimate goal you are seeking? Where are you trying to reach? This should be clarified to the House. The House also belongs to the government. It is the supreme forum of the people. The supreme forum cannot be deceived. If the Honorable Prime Minister continues to deceive in this manner, then the Honorable Prime Minister will also have to answer. Where were you born? Where is your birthplace? I want to ask this through you, Honorable Chairperson. I would like to conclude by saying this. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai, you have 9 minutes. (13:50 PM) After this, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal. Honorable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, on the 4th of Jestha, the Chairman of Gurans Rural Municipality in Dailekh district wrote a circular to the Chief District Officer of the same district requesting necessary action. I also received that circular on my WhatsApp. It seemed normal at first glance, but upon closer inspection, it seemed quite serious and sensitive. The Raute community, who had been permanently residing in Gurans Rural Municipality of that district, and who used to live a nomadic life in their surrounding districts, were taken to Morang district, my own province, for a Raute community festival and fair. A tourism organization, without coordinating with any local people, and without involving the main leaders of the Raute community, who are called 'Mukhia', took them to Banke and Bardia by deceiving them and putting them in vehicles. Upon reaching there, the objective was to display their handicrafts and exchange cultures. This sounds very good, as if it is in favor of the backward class and community of the Raute people. But it was not done according to the objective. What was done there was that they were kept in Miklajung Rural Municipality, and they were dressed up every day. 19 young men and women, girls, were displayed in their traditional attire. I have a picture of this. They were displayed, and not only displayed, but tickets were sold at Rs. 200, and funds were also collected. Therefore, this caused controversy and protest from all sides. This was an extremely serious matter, and something that no one, no community, could accept. That is why I want to urge, Honorable Chairperson, no matter who they are, they are human beings. They are not a means of display, and every community, whether large or small, whether powerful or poor, has its own religion, culture, traditions, and customs. And these customs and cultures cannot be sold by anyone, nor can they be used as a source of income by anyone. The state itself cannot do this today, nor can society. However, if we look at it positively, I saw them at the fair. I saw them enjoying themselves at the fair. When journalists asked them if they were happy, they said they were happy and enjoying themselves, poor things, not knowing that their dignity, their honor, their traditions, their self-respect were being hurt today. They did not know that. Therefore, I want to draw the attention of the government, through you, Honorable Chairperson, to this incident. What is the matter? The truth should be investigated. If they were indeed used in that manner, then those responsible should be brought to justice. Honorable Chairperson, the issue is not new, it is old. We have raised it here repeatedly. The problem of the landless, which is not being solved today, is becoming more complicated. The government is silent today. According to government data, 35,026 houses have been demolished today, and 19 settlements have been destroyed. More than 300,000 people have had their homes demolished, and they have been relocated to various places. They have been taken to temples and churches. We went to see a holding center in the name of a holding center, the Ichchhu Narayan holding center. The situation is extremely tragic. And truly speaking, no one with a heart and feelings can bear to see that scene. No one can control their emotions. For what purpose was the Janji movement launched today, to rule over the tears of the poor, the helpless, and the landless? For what change did the Janji people fight today? Today, I want to ask the government, Balen's government. What would you have done? Don't we understand? What did you do when your wife had a slight problem with the car while taking her to the hospital? Don't we understand that? Therefore, with the spirit you are currently showing, please take steps towards a solution with the same speed. Otherwise, do not force this movement and push the country into a state of confrontation. And various problems have arisen there. Many problems are about to arise. Two people have already committed suicide. Not two, many are on the verge of suicide today. Many people are in a state of depression today. Chronically ill patients are dying due to lack of treatment. Do you want to watch this spectacle? I hear on social media that it was done correctly. Some people are enjoying it. Is this something to enjoy? People are living on the verge of death. Is this something to enjoy? I want to tell you all. Do not apply balm to others' pain. Do not talk about enjoyment. Be careful, as the tiger that eats me might eat you too. I urge everyone. And today, movements have arisen everywhere. I want to say in their language: Give us land, government, not money. Give us land, and give us a place to live, not displacement. And let the poor, helpless people live. I also want to urge the government with their demands. Many people have placed great expectations on you. This is not to see this plight. Please keep this in mind. And just now, a serious issue of border dispute between Humla and Bajura has led to clashes and physical altercations. If this escalates, it is also a serious matter. We have heard that if it escalates, there will be many more such negative incidents. Therefore, I urge the government to find out the truth and move towards resolving this problem in a timely manner. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal, you have 5 minutes. (13:59 PM) After this, Honorable Member Durga Gurung. Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dangal (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, due to the time constraint, I would like to directly enter into the subject matter. The government can bring ordinances under Article 114 of the Constitution. This time, the government has brought eight ordinances, including an ordinance related to the Constitutional Council, its functions, duties, and procedures. Ordinances must be tabled in the first meeting of the Parliament after its convening. The government is aware of this. Ordinances brought in this manner become ineffective if they are not approved by both houses of the Parliament within a certain time limit. The government is also well aware of this. I am not raising the issue here regarding the process, context, and content of these ordinances. I will express my views and opinions once the ordinances are presented in the House and the discussion process begins. After the government tabled these eight ordinances in the National Assembly, the agenda was to discuss and present them for decision on the 7th of Jestha, 2083. The honorable members of the House were also informed to submit a notice of rejection if they did not agree with the ordinances. Accordingly, the honorable members registered their notices of rejection with reasons in the prescribed format. However, in the meantime, the meeting of the House on the 7th of Jestha was adjourned. On the day when the ordinances were scheduled for discussion and decision. On one hand, there is no business to run the House, and we have adjourned meetings repeatedly. On the other hand, matters that were on the agenda, had progressed in the discussion process, and the process had moved forward. I say the process had moved forward in the sense that notices of rejection were given, and the honorable members had prepared for it. This process had moved forward. Discussions were ongoing, and in the meantime, it was adjourned. Is this not a contradiction? On one hand, it was adjourned due to lack of business, and on the other hand, there was...

Agenda items, proposals withdrawn, and the parliament was adjourned. This is the situation. Therefore, regarding this ordinance, for what reasons was the meeting adjourned on the day the ordinance was to be discussed? When will these ordinances be discussed and decided upon? This is also a matter of public concern. It is also a matter that has been tabled here. It is also a matter of general discussion. Therefore, I wanted to request with humility. I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal and the Honourable Chairperson for information to the Business Advisory Committee meeting. On the other hand, the rules provide for Zero Hour, Emergency Hour, and Special Hour. The country's situation, local problems, national political issues, economic matters, development contexts, and various other issues have been raised and discussed by the Honourable Members. However, these have become neglected. They have become neglected. So far, not a single Honourable Minister has appeared in this House to respond to them. Therefore, I want to make a strong demand immediately.
